The user asks: "is chrome is installed". They want to check if Chrome is installed. We need to use the tool to run a command. On Windows, we can check via registry or existence of path. Let's try to check typical installation paths: C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe or C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe. We'll attempt to check existence. Use dir command? Or test file existence. In Windows, we can use 'if exist' command. But we can just list directory and see if it contains chrome.exe. Let's do something like:

cmd: 'dir "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" >nul 2>&1 && echo found || echo notfound'

But we can't capture output easily; the function returns whatever os.system returns. That might not give us output. Alternatively, we could use 'where chrome.exe', which will search PATH. But Chrome may not be in PATH. So better to check known directories.

We can chain two checks: first Program Files (x86), then Program Files. Use '||' to combine. Something like:

'if exist "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" (echo found) else if exist "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" (echo found) else (echo notfound)'

But Windows batch syntax: 'if exist ... (echo found) else (echo notfound)' works only one else. We can chain: 'if exist ... (echo found) else if exist ... (echo found) else (echo notfound)'. That should work.

Let's construct command: 'if exist "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" (echo found) else if exist "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" (echo found) else (echo notfound)'
